short: A formal order to a supplier stating what you agreed to buy.
seoTitle: Purchase Order — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A purchase order is a document sent to a supplier specifying items, quantities, agreed rates, delivery date and terms. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: A purchase order is a document sent to a supplier specifying items, quantities, agreed rates, delivery date and terms. Accepted, it becomes the commercial agreement the delivery and invoice are checked against.
bodyHtml:
Why Purchase Order matters

Without a PO, disputes come down to memory. It is also the only clean way to catch a supplier billing above the agreed rate, which is common and rarely deliberate.

How Purchase Order works in practice

Raise a numbered PO for anything above a threshold you set, and match the invoice to it before payment. Where rates were negotiated verbally, the PO is what records them.

faq.question: Do small businesses need purchase orders?
faq.answer: For regular suppliers and larger values, yes. The discipline pays for itself the first time a rate is billed wrongly.

faq.question: What if the supplier delivers more than ordered?
faq.answer: Record the actual receipt, and either return the excess or agree a revised order — do not pay on the invoice alone.
